frames.narration: A team finishes training version 7 of a fraud-scoring model. It uploads the 4 GB weights to the artifact store in resumable chunks, and registers the version with its lineage: code commit, data snapshot, hyperparameters and training metrics.
The version is immutable from this moment, and uploading the same bytes again would return v7 again. Moving it to staging starts the evaluation jobs on the real GPU type.
Accuracy is 93.1 percent against 92.5 for production, and p95 latency is 88 ms, under the limit of 120 ms. Both gates pass, so v7 may be proposed for production.

A second person, who is not the author, approves the promotion. The registry writes an audit record: who, when, which evaluation and which version v7 replaces. Then it asks the builder for a serving image.

The builder produces a small image with the pinned runtime and signs it. The weights are fetched by hash, checked against the checksum, and kept in the node cache, so the next replica on that node starts without downloading.
A calling service sends a scoring request. The router hashes the caller's id, which keeps each caller on one version, and sends 5 percent of callers to v7 and 95 percent to v6.

After half an hour the per-version metrics show v7 with an error rate of 0.2 percent and a p95 of 88 ms, the same as v6, and no drift in its outputs. The router steps the canary to 25 percent, then 50, then 100.
v6 stays loaded for a while after the switch. If a problem shows up, the router moves the weights back in seconds, with no build and no download, and the audit trail records why.
